o: Two brands, one Next.js codebase. Pureairo for Russell across NSW, EcoHealth for Steve in Melbourne. Different colours, contacts, geography, leak-tested.
l: Brand differentiation lives below the surface: contact data, postcode bias, even WCAG ratios. Abstracted into one config or the whole thing leaks.
challenge: Russell ran Pureairo in Sydney. Steve ran a sister business in Melbourne. Both needed brand-grade sites with separate domains and a shared service backbone. The trap was a single codebase that quietly leaks each brand into the other, sending Sydney enquiries to Melbourne and vice versa.
solutions: Host-header middleware resolves each domain to a brand context (x-brand), threaded through every Next.js server component
Two visually distinct identities sharing one design system, Pureairo green and EcoHealth blue, both hand-tuned to WCAG AA 4.5:1 on white
Full collateral system, business cards, A-frames, car magnets, door-hanger flyers, all brand-aware via the same config
180-test E2E brand-leak suite, axe-core plus Playwright, catches any visible Pureairo string on an EcoHealth page (or the reverse) before it ships

stats.l: Brands served from one codebase
